notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, from the Report of Local Government Finance filed with the Department of Community Affairs (audited figures). Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.

Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric, gas, airport and other enterprise funds. Debt service counts long-term principal retired and interest; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($3,829,831) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing, planning and economic development count as overhead.
Debt is revenue bonds, general obligation bonds, other long-term debt, capital leases, special assessment debt and short-term notes outstanding at year end.
Political money is not scored: Georgia county candidates file their campaign reports with the county election superintendent, not with a statewide agency.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Georgia yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Oconee County Sheriff's Office operates 24 Flock Safety automated license plate readers as of September 2025.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS017541, citing Public Records From the EFF via Pittsboro Police - See note

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Oconee County Sheriff's Office operates one drone, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003655, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

Public schools are run by separate school districts, and Oconee County provides many other services; residents pay the city, the county and the school district.

Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric, gas, airport and other enterprise funds. Debt service counts long-term principal retired and interest; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($56,201) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing, planning and economic development count as overhead.
Debt is revenue bonds, general obligation bonds, other long-term debt, capital leases, special assessment debt and short-term notes outstanding at year end.
Political money is not scored: Georgia city candidates file their campaign reports with the city clerk, not with a statewide agency.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 2 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Watkinsville's borders in OpenStreetMap (2 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Georgia yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 2 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Watkinsville's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Watkinsville Police Department got approval from the Georgia Department of Transportation in November 2021 to install seven automated license plate readers.
